issues.description: HAS_PERCENTAGE regex omits the case-insensitive flag while HAS_KEYWORD includes it, creating asymmetric and undocumented behavior.
issues.detail: In keyframe-selector-notation, HAS_KEYWORD uses /i but HAS_PERCENTAGE does not. While percentages are digit-only and case is moot for the literal, the asymmetry has no stated justification. CSS treats keyframe tokens like from/to case-insensitively. State the invariant or normalize the flags so the two branches share a uniform contract.

issues.description: Using `/./` as a match-everything sentinel in walkRules is an abstraction leak and bad taste.
issues.detail: The walkRules filter accepts a regex; passing `/./` to mean 'no filter' is clever-instead-of-obvious and leaks implementation detail into the caller's contract. Cleaner: branch on whether a filter exists and call walkRules(cb) vs walkRules(regex, cb). Same behavior, clearer intent for the next maintainer.

issues.description: Font-weight HAS_NAMED/HAS_NUMERIC regexes have inconsistent case-sensitivity and lack escaping/over-approximation spec.
issues.detail: HAS_NAMED uses /i but HAS_NUMERIC does not, and the keyword arrays are joined raw into the RegExp source. The numeric `\b(?:100|...|900)\b` may match inside var()/calc() fallbacks. As a fast-reject prefilter it must over-approximate the slow path; pick one case stance and add a comment stating the precondition.

issues.description: import-notation `url` branch inverts filter polarity vs siblings without a documenting comment.
issues.detail: For primary === 'url', the code returns when `url(` IS present — the opposite of sibling branches. The logic is correct (violation = string-form when url expected) but the asymmetry is easy to misread and 'fix.' Extract the regex to a const matching sibling files and add a one-line spec comment per branch stating what each filter admits.

issues.description: selector-pseudo-element-colon-notation `/:/` prefilter is too permissive to deliver meaningful perf gains.
issues.detail: walkRules(/:/) matches any selector containing a colon — every :hover, :focus, :is(), attribute selectors with colons, and namespace prefixes. The change is semantically equivalent to the prior `selector.includes(':')` check and consistent with sibling selector-* rules, but the perf benefit is marginal. Acceptable; just don't oversell it.

issues.description: No new tests or shared abstraction for the fast-reject prefilter pattern now spanning six rules.
issues.detail: The same idiom — 'compile presence regex, bail early if absent' — is reinvented across six rules with no named contract or boundary tests. The over-approximation invariant (fast-path rejection must imply slow-path rejection) is implicit. Add targeted boundary tests per rule and either factor a shared quickReject helper or document the convention in a comment.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a sound performance optimization: cheap presence-check prefilters added ahead of expensive valueParser/selector walks across six *-notation rules. The shared concern is that the emerging fast-reject pattern has an unstated contract — the prefilter must over-approximate the slow path — and that contract is violated or undocumented in several places. Concrete fixes: resolve the HAS_PERCENTAGE/HAS_KEYWORD case-flag asymmetry, replace the `/./` sentinel with a clean branch, and add a spec comment naming the over-approximation invariant. Lands with minor cleanup; no correctness blocker found.
